## 1. HTTP error responses are accepted as successful data

**Severity:** High
**Class:** correctness

Both providers consider `client.Do` success sufficient and decode the body without checking `StatusCode`. Grafana commonly returns valid JSON error objects for 401/404; decoding into the payload struct succeeds while unknown fields are ignored, so `Fetch` returns an empty dashboard. A Graphite 5xx body containing `[]` likewise becomes an empty successful metric set. Core reports can therefore show zero data when upstream rejected the request.

**Fix.** Accept only documented 2xx statuses. For others, close the body and return a typed error with status and a bounded sanitized excerpt; retry suitable 429/5xx responses. Test 401, 404, 429, 500 and empty bodies for both providers.

## 2. Cache entries cross Graphite endpoints and time windows

**Severity:** High
**Class:** correctness

The cache filename is derived only from metric prefix. Lookup ignores both Graphite endpoint and the `last` duration, and accepts a hit for one day. Production and staging with the same prefix, or one-hour and one-week queries, reuse the first result without contacting the requested service. The user receives a plausible but wrong metric universe and coverage report.

**Fix.** Namespace cache by a versioned hash of canonical endpoint identity, prefix, time window, and every result-affecting option. Persist/verify key metadata and keep credentials out of paths/logs. Test endpoint and duration cache misses.

## 3. User-controlled glob syntax can crash normal CLI commands

**Severity:** Med
**Class:** correctness

Filter and exclusion flags, autocomplete text, and REPL queries call `model.Query(...).MustCompile()`. Invalid glob syntax panics instead of returning a validation error. Batch commands crash after network/cache work; in REPL one malformed line ends the session through top-level panic recovery.

**Fix.** Expose non-panicking `Compile() (Matcher, error)`, validate flags during `PreRunE`, and have REPL paths report the error and continue. Reserve `MustCompile` for constants and add malformed syntax tests.

## 4. Malformed configuration files are silently ignored

**Severity:** Med
**Class:** build

`WithConfig` handles only a successful `.env.paas` read and `os.IsNotExist`; syntax, permission, and other errors fall through. The `app.toml` fallback also merges only on success and silently discards parse failures. Commands continue with environment/default values, causing misleading missing-setting errors or contacting a different service than intended.

**Fix.** Return every read/parse/merge/unmarshal error with its filename; fall back only when the primary file truly does not exist. Replace request-time `fn.Must` with error propagation and test malformed, unreadable, and mistyped configuration.

## 5. Graphite tree traversal has no concurrency bound

**Severity:** Med
**Class:** perf

Every non-leaf starts a goroutine, and each recursive call creates another errgroup with the same behavior. A wide namespace can generate thousands of simultaneous requests, goroutines, progress updates, and response bodies. HTTP timeout bounds duration but not fan-out, risking socket/memory exhaustion and Graphite overload.

**Fix.** Use a bounded worker pool or shared semaphore with configurable conservative concurrency. Keep one cancellation group, deduplicate visited nodes, and test a synthetic wide/deep tree while asserting maximum in-flight requests.

## 6. Cache reads and rewrites are unsynchronized

**Severity:** Med
**Class:** concurrency

All commands for a prefix open the same temp file read/write, decode it, then truncate and rewrite in place. There is no process lock, keyed mutex, or atomic replacement. Concurrent invocations can read partial JSON, interleave writes, corrupt future calls, and stampede the provider after reading the same expired value.

**Fix.** Serialize fills per key, use an inter-process lock when processes share files, and write a temporary file followed by sync/close/atomic rename. Treat corrupt content as a quarantined miss and add concurrent/interrupted-write tests.
